intro: Paired representations identify one matching key per query. The other keys in the batch become negative candidates, so the loss depends on both pair alignment and batch composition.
task: Compute one-directional InfoNCE with the diagonal query-key pairs as positives. Inspect how a smaller temperature changes separation when matches are correct or incorrect.
requirements: queries and keys have the same nonempty shape (N,D). Every row must have L2 norm one, checked with rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8. Do not silently normalize inputs.
Require a finite temperature >=1e-6. Scores are queries@keys.T/temperature; the positive score for row i is score[i,i].
Return mean(logsumexp(scores[i,:])-scores[i,i]) using shifted logits. This is one-directional in-batch InfoNCE, not a symmetric CLIP loss or the full SimCLR batching scheme.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Build the whole comparison matrix
hints.body: Elementwise row dot products alone omit the negative candidates in the denominator.

hints.title: Keep the diagonal aligned
hints.body: The same reordering of queries and keys preserves matches; reordering only one side generally does not.

explanation: Duplicated keys create indistinguishable candidates. Identical unit vectors on both sides can therefore still have loss log(N); alignment alone does not guarantee a near-zero loss.
Lower temperature sharpens the distribution. It helps when the positive score is largest and can amplify an incorrect match, so it does not universally reduce loss.
Adapted the upstream one-directional objective with explicit unit-vector checks, a documented temperature floor and shifted log probabilities. No encoder training is simulated.
